tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Transitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi le somno (lungo somno).
I slept (a long sleep).

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Transitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Yu le haha (sotipul haha).
You laughed (a loud laugh).

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Transitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Kam yu fleygi hawanavi?
Do you fly aircraft?

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Transitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi xa sampogi bwaw fe axam.
I will walk the dog in the evening.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Transitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Payaco le hahagi mi.
The clown made me laugh.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Intransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Navikef le garaku.
The captain drowned.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Intransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Navikef le garaku**(**gi**) **navi.
The captain sank the ship.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Basalogi interes mi.
Linguistics interests me.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi interes tem basalogi.** = **Mi sen interesdo tem basalogi.
I'm interested in linguistics.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Tesu ergo pilo te.
Her work tires her.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Te pilo.** = **Te sen pilodo.
She is tired.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi le interes tem basalogi lefe multi nyan.** = **Mi le sen interesdo tem basalogi lefe multi nyan.
I was interested in linguistics many years ago.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Te le pilo dur na ergo.** = **Te le sen pilodo dur na ergo.
She was tired while working.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi le interescu** (or **xorinteres**) **tem basalogi lefe multi nyan.** = **Mi le sencu** (or **xorsen**) **interesdo tem basalogi lefe multi nyan.
I became interested in linguistics many years ago.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Te le pilocu** (or **xorpilo**) **dur na ergo.** = **Te le sencu** (or **xorsen**) **pilodo dur na ergo.
She got/became tired while working.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Kam yu le termo banyo-kamer?
Did you warm up the bathroom?

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Misu kafe no haji termo. = Misu kafe no haji sen termopul.
My coffee isn't hot any longer.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Eskol le cinon te.
The school made him smart.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Syensiyen cinon. = Syensiyen sen cinonpul.
The scientist is intelligent.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Patre le talento lalayen.
The father made the singer talented.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Lalayen talento. = Lalayen sen talentopul.
The singer is talented.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Jaledin le termo. = Jaledin le sen termopul.
Yesterday was warm.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: To le termocu** (or **xortermo**) **fe midi-nuru.** = **To le sencu** (or **xorsen**) **termopul fe midi-nuru.
It got/became warm at noon.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi le kasiru janela.
I broke the window.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Janela le kasiru**(**cu**)**.
The window broke.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Te le boyle sui.
She boiled the water.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Sui le boyle**(**cu**)**.
The water boiled.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Ete le fini jange.
They ended the war.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Jange le fini**(**cu**)**.
The war ended.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Am esto mobil!
Stop the car!

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Am esto**(**cu**)**!
Stop!

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi le harka yusu kursi.
I moved your chair.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Am no harka**(**cu**)**!
Don't move!

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Mi le buka dwer.
I opened the door.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Dwer le buka**(**cu**)**.
The door opened.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Hinto sen _bon yam_.
This is a _good meal_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Bebe _bon yam_.
The baby _eats well_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Uma _velosi pawbu_.
The horse _runs fast_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Bebe yam _bon_.
The baby eats _well_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Bwaw glu sui _velosi_.
The dog drinks the water _quickly_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: _Velosi_, bwaw glu sui.
_Quickly_, the dog drinks the water.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: _Unyum_, te le idi cel banko.
_First_, she went to the bank.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Doxone,_ nini le xorsomno.
_Reading,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Fe na doxo,_ nini le xorsomno.
_Reading,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Dur na doxo,_ nini le xorsomno.
_While reading,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Dur na doxo sesu preferido kitabu,_ nini le xorsomno.
_While reading his favorite book,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Durki te le doxo (sesu preferido kitabu),_ nini le xorsomno.
_While he read (his favorite book),_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: Baytu de Maria sen day.
"House of Mary is big."

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: To de Maria sen day.
Mary's is big.

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: Maria su baytu sen day.
Mary's house is big.

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: Maria su to sen day.
Mary's is big.

tu.note: Pronouns > Third-Person Pronouns at End of Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Multi _te_ pala sol in Englisa.
Many (_people_) speak only (in) English.

tu.note: Pronouns > Third-Person Pronouns at End of Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: bon _te_, bur _te_ ji colo _te_
the good (_one_), the bad (_one_) and the ugly (_one_)
Hinto bon nasacu.
This (thing) smells good.
Hin bon nasacu... memorigi mi cel misu femgami.
This good smell... reminds me of my wife.
Kenumer te bon lala?
How many (of them) sing well?
Mi le kari dua kilogramo fe risi. Yu le kari kekwanti to?
I bought two kilos of rice. How much did you buy?

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku fe ke mesi.
I know in what month.

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Te le no loga ku keseba.
She didn't say why.

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Dento sen ku keloka.
That is where.

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku na idi keloka.
I know where to go.
Mi ergo** _**denloka hu yu ergo**_**.
I work _where you work_.
Mi xa preata** _**denwatu hu yam sen jumbi**_**.** _or_ _**Denwatu hu yam sen jumbi,**_ **mi xa preata.
I will arrive _when the meal is ready_.
Mi xa preata** _**denwatu hu yam sen jumbi**_**.** _or_ _**Denwatu hu yam sen jumbi,**_ **mi xa preata.
_When the meal is ready_, I will arrive.
Mi le no idi cel parti** _**denseba hu yu idi**_**.
I didn't go to the party _for the reason that you went_.
Mi le xuli mobil** _**denmaner hu yu le alim tas mi**_**.
I fixed the car _how/like you taught me_.
Yu** _**daydenmo**_ **bala.
You are _so_ strong.
Yu hare** _**daydenmo**_ **day oko.
You have _such_ big eyes.
Mi le kari tiga yuxitul tas** _**moyun nini**_**.
I bought three toys for _each child_.
Mi le kari tiga yuxitul tas** _**moy nini**_**.
I bought three toys for _all the children_.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Mi no dupul oko te xorfe mesi tiga.
I haven't seen her since March.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul kone te dur 30 nyan.
I have known him for 30 years.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul sen gadibu.
I have been angry.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Yu dupul sen kepul?
How have you been?

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Perfect Progressive in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul yam hin pingo dur un satu.
I have been eating this apple for one hour.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Perfect Progressive in English

tuv.seg: Yu dupul fale keto?
What have you been doing?

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Perfect Progressive in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul doxo hin kitabu xorfe jaleli sabedin.
I have been reading this book since last week.
Mi ger yam pingo eger mi sen yamkal.
I would eat the apple if I were hungry.
Myaw le no velosi yam piu.
The cat didn't eat the bird quickly.
Piu le no velosi beyam myaw.
The bird wasn't quickly eaten by the cat.
Mi vole bwaw, mas te am no sen godomo day.
I want a dog, but it should/must not be too big.
Mi hare gutonpul denta; mi am idi cel dentamedisyen.
I have a painful tooth; I need to go to the dentist.
Mi vole ki te am safegi sesu kamer.
I want him to clean his room.
Mi peti ki imi am xorata jaldi.
I ask that we arrive early.
Kitabu hu xwexiyen am doxo da no sen daymo lungo.
The book that the pupils are to read is not very long.
Kam yu am sahay mi?
Could you help me?
Kam yu am klosi janela?
Would you (kindly) close the window.
Eger mi xa yam pingo, mi xa no haji sen yamkal.
If I eat the apple (_in the future_), I will no longer be hungry.
Eger te le yam yusu pingo, kam yu xa sen gadibu?
If he ate your apple (_in the past_), will you be angry?
Eger te yam yusu pingo, kam yu gadibucu?
If he eats your apples (_in general_), do you get angry?

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Determiner + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: _Banete_ ergo velosi ji _banete_ ergo hanman.
_Some_ work quickly and _some_ work slowly.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Determiner + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Ban ergo sen velosi ji ban ergo sen hanman.
Some work is fast and some work is slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Possessive Adj + Pronoun (Possessive Pronoun) = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Yusu gami ergo velosi mas _misu_ te ergo hanman.
Your spouse works fast but _mine_ works slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Possessive Adj + Pronoun (Possessive Pronoun) = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Misu ergo sen hanman.
My work/job is slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Quantifier + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Dua basataytiyen ergo velosi mas _un te_ ergo hanman.
Two translators work quickly but _one_ works slowly.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Quantifier + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Un ergo sen hanman.
One job is slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adjective + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Day manyen ergo velosi mas _lil te_ ergo hanman.
The big man works quickly but the _small one_ works slowly.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adjective + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Lil ergo sen hanman.
The small job is slow.
Femyen danse _meli_.
The lady dances _beautifully_.
Mi le gibe pesa tas coriyen _volekal_ koski mi le befobi ki te xa morgi mi.
I gave the money to the thief _involuntarily_ because I feared he would kill me.
Manyen _no godomo bur_ danse.
or: **Manyen danse _no godomo bur_.**
Manixu _no danse godomo bur_.
The man _doesn't dance too badly_.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adverbs of Focus

tuv.seg: Misu gami glu _sol_ kafe fe soba.
My spouse drinks _only_ coffee in the morning.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adverbs of Focus

tuv.seg: Misu gami glu kafe _hata_ fe axam.
My spouse drinks coffee _even_ in the evening.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adverbs of Focus

tuv.seg: _Pia_ misu gami glu kafe fe soba.
My spouse, _too_, drinks coffee in the morning.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Complex Adjective Phrases

tuv.seg: kitabu eskrido fal misu doste
the book written by my friend

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Complex Adjective Phrases

tuv.seg: alimyen hox kos yusu sukses
the teacher happy for your success

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Complex Adjective Phrases

tuv.seg: nini maxmo lao kom misu sodar
the kid older than my brother

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen femixu _hu da lubi mi_.
"She is the woman _who that-one loves me_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen femixu _hu mi lubi da_.
"She is the woman _who I love that-one_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Mi le sonxi katatul _hu mi kata roti yon da_.
"I lost the knife _which I cut the bread with that-one_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Kamisa _hu mi suki da_ sen blue.** or **To sen blue, kamisa _hu mi suki da_.
"The shirt _which I like that-one_ is blue." or "It's blue, the shirt _which I like that-one_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen manixu _hu dasu sodar kone mi_.
"He is the man _who his brother knows me._"

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen manixu _hu mi kone dasu sodar_.
"He is the man _who I know his brother_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_ sen misu doste.** _or_ **Te sen misu doste, manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_.
"The guy _who that-one's spouse speaks Globasa_ is my friend."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_ sen misu doste.** _or_ **Te sen misu doste, manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_.
"He's my friend, the guy _who that one's spouse speaks Globasa_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu mi ergo denloka_ sen day.
"The library _which I work there_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu denloka mi ergo_ sen day.
"The library _which there I work_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu mi xa preata denwatu_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which I arrive then_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu denwatu mi xa preata_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which then I arrive_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu mi ergo in da_ sen day.
"The library _which I work in it_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu in da mi ergo_ sen day.
"The library _which in it I work_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu mi xa preata fe da_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which I arrive on it_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu fe da mi xa preata_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which on it I arrive_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _to hu mi ergo denloka_.
"I don't like _it which I work there_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _to hu denloka mi ergo_.
"I don't like _it which there I work_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _to hu yu broxa misu tofa denmaner_.
"I like _it which you brush my hair that way_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _to hu denmaner yu broxa misu tofa_.
"I like _it which that way you brush my hair_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Am gibe tas mi _to hu mi vole da_.
"Give me _it which I want that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _te hu yu le seleti da_.
"I don't like _her/him/them who you chose that-one._"

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _loka hu mi ergo in da_.
"I don't like _the place which I work in that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _loka hu in da mi ergo_.
"I don't like _the place which in that I work_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _maner hu yu broxa misu tofa yon da_.
"I like _the way which you brush my hair in that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _maner hu yon da yu broxa misu tofa_.
"I like _the way which in that you brush my hair_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Am gibe tas mi _xey hu mi vole da_.
"Give me _the thing which I want that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _person hu yu le seleti da_.
"I don't like _the person who you chose that-one._"

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Non-relative Modifying Clauses

tuv.seg: Singa begude idey _feki maux ger abil na sahay te_.
The lion was tickled by the idea _that the mouse could help him_.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _restoran feki imi le yam_.
"I don't like _the restaurant that we ate at_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: Te sokutu _(fe) moy mara feki te estaycu_.
"He falls every time that he stands up."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: Mi suki _maner feki yu broxa misu tofa_.
"I like _the way that you brush my hair_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: _Seba feki yu no xwexi_ sen koski yu no abyasa.
"The reason that you don't learn is because you don't practice."
Myaw sen keloka?
Where is the cat?

(In Globasa), you say...

I love you.
Multi te pala sol in Englisa.
Many (people) speak only (in) English.
bon te, bur te ji colo te
the good (one), the bad (one) and the ugly (one)
Hinto bon nasacu.
This (thing) smells good.
Hin bon nasacu... memorigi mi cel misu femgami.
This good smell... reminds me of my wife.
Kenumer te bon lala?
How many (of them) sing well?
Mi le kari dua kilogramo fe risi. Yu le kari kekwanti to?
I bought two kilos of rice. How much did you buy?
Kete lubi yu?
Who loves you?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I know this: Who loves you?.")

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku kete lubi yu.
I know who loves you.
Yu lubi kete?
Who(m) do you love?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I know this: You love who(m)?.")

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku yu lubi kete.
I know who(m) you love.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "He wants to eat what?")

tuv.seg: Te vole na yam keto?
What does he want to eat?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I forgot this: He wants to eat what?.")

tuv.seg: Mi le wanji ku te vole na yam keto.
I forgot what he wants to eat.
Te le gibe pesa tas ke doste?
"She gave the money to which friend?" Which friend did she give the money to?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "She didn't say this Which friend did she give the money to?.")

tuv.seg: Te le no loga ku te le gibe pesa tas ke doste.
She didn't say which friend she gave the money to.
Hinto sen kesu kursi?
Whose chair is this?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I want to know this: This is whose chair?.")

tuv.seg: Mi vole na jixi ku hinto sen kesu kursi.
I want to know whose chair this is.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "Whose book on the table?")

tuv.seg: Kesu kitabu sen per mesa?
Whose book is on the table.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I know this: Whose book is on the table?.")

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku kesu kitabu sen per mesa.
I know whose book is on the table.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "She asked this: You are how?.")

tuv.seg: Te le swal ku yu sen kepul.
She asked how you were.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "You are what kind of person?")

tuv.seg: Yu sen kepul insan?
What kind of person are you?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I know this: What kind of person are you?.")

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku yu sen kepul insan.

Te sen kemo lao?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "She told me this: She is how old?.")

tuv.seg: Te le loga tas mi ku te sen kemo lao.
She told me how old she is.
Yu sen kemo pilodo?
How tired are you?
Mi jixi ku yu sen kemo pilodo.
I know this: "You are how tired?".

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "You bought how much rice?")

tuv.seg: Yu le kari kekwanti risi?
How much rice did you buy?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I saw this: You bought how much rice?.")

tuv.seg: Mi le oko ku yu le kari kekwanti risi.
I saw how much rice you bought.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "You have how many children?")

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I wonder this: You have how many children?.")

Te ergo keloka?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I know this: He works where?.")

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku te ergo keloka.
I know where he works.
Te xa preata kewatu?
When will she arrive?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "That is this: She will arrive when?.")

tuv.seg: Dento sen ku te xa preata kewatu.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "You didn't go to the party why?")

tuv.seg: Yu le no idi cel parti keseba?

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "I know this: You didn't go to the party why?.")

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku yu le no idi cel parti keseba.
I know why you didn't go to the party.

tu.note: Gramati: tabellexi (lit. "You fixed the car how?")

tuv.seg: Yu le xuli mobil kemaner?
How did you fix the car?
Mi jixivole ku yu le xuli mobil kemaner.
I wonder this: You fixed the car how?."
Mi jixi ku fe ke mesi.
I know in what month.
Te le no loga ku keseba.
She didn't say why.
Dento sen ku keloka.
That is where.
Mi jixi ku na idi keloka.
I know where to go.
Mi ergo denloka hu yu ergo.
I work where you work.
Denwatu hu yam sen jumbi, mi xa preata.
I will arrive when the meal is ready. or When the meal is ready, I will arrive.
Mi le no idi cel parti denseba hu yu idi.
I didn't go to the party for the reason that you went.
Mi le xuli mobil denmaner hu yu le alim tas mi.
I fixed the car how/like you taught me.
Denmaner hu mi le loga...
Like I said...
Mi sen hazuni kom yu.
I am sad like you.
Mi sen denpul kom yu.
I am like you.
Mi salom yu sodarsim kom misu sodar.
I greet you fraternally as my brother.
Mi salom yu denpul kom misu sodar.
I greet you as my brother.
Mi no abil na lala meli kom yu.
I can't sing beautifully like you.
Mi no abil na lala denpul kom yu.
I can't sing like you.
Sama kom mi, pia te hare tiga bete.
The same as me, she too has three children.
Denpul kom mi, pia te hare tiga bete.
Like me, she too has three children.
Hin baytu sen daymo day kom misu to.
This house is very big like mine.
Hin baytu sen denmo day kom misu to.
This house is as big as mine.
Mi hare tiga bete kom misu gami.
I have three children like my spouse.
Mi hare dennumer bete kom misu gami.
I have as many children as my spouse.
Mi le kari dua kilogramo fe risi kom yu.
I bought two kilos of rice like you.
Mi le kari denkwanti risi kom yu.
I bought as much rice as you.
Daydenpul din!
What a day!
Yu daydenmo bala.
You are so strong.
Yu hare daydenmo day oko.
You have such big eyes.
Daydenmo meli!
How beautiful!
Daydenmo meli din!
What a beautiful day!
Mi le kari tiga yuxitul cel moyun nini.
I bought three toys for each child.
Mi le kari tiga yuxitul cel moy nini.
I bought three toys for all the children.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Consider the sentence-initial use of ban din (some day or some days) in the following example sentences. Notice how if we want to say "some days" we can still just say ban din without the need to introduce plu since the verb form (with or without du-, or present vs past/future) would indicate whether we're speaking about a general habit (plural) or a one-time occurrence.

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi jagecu dyer.
Some days I wake up late. (present tense: habitual)

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Notice how if we want to say "some days" we can still just say ban din without the need to introduce plu since the verb form (with or without du-, or present vs past/future) would indicate whether we're speaking about a general habit (plural) or a one-time occurrence. Some days I wake up late. (present tense: habitual)

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi le dujagecu dyer.
Some days, I would wake up late.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Some days I wake up late. (present tense: habitual) Some days, I would wake up late. (du-: habitual)

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi xa loga tas te satiya.
Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Some days, I would wake up late. (du-: habitual) Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth.

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi le loga tas te satiya.
One day, I told him the truth.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] On the other hand, it has occurred to me that it would be useful for the numeral un to be used as a determiner to mean "a certain". This is in contrast to ban, which is ambiguous and can be either singular or plural. Using un in place of ban to mark singularity doesn't add an extra word, making its systematic use less awkward than the repetitive use of plu to mark plurality would, since plu adds a word rather than replaces. So the last two example sentences above could also be expressed using un din instead of ban din:

tuv.seg: Un din, mi xa loga tas te satiya.
Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] So the last two example sentences above could also be expressed using un din instead of ban din: Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth

tuv.seg: Un din, mi le loga tas te satiya.
One day, I told him the truth.

tu.note: [yamgi vs yamgibe] Now, the problem with the direct object of yamgi potentially working either way is that if there's only one argument, we should probably assume it's the recipient (Mi le yamgi myaw), but what if it's not? What if we actually intend for it to be the patient? In that case, using yamgibe would work best to avoid confusion (Mi le yamgibe maux). If we really wanted to express a more forceful causation, depending on the context and intended meaning (degree of agency or intentionality), we could use verbs like musigi, pel, lide (?) (and others).

tuv.seg: Opera pel te na wawa.
Opera makes her cry. ("Opera drives her to tears.")

tu.note: [yamgi vs yamgibe] If we really wanted to express a more forceful causation, depending on the context and intended meaning (degree of agency or intentionality), we could use verbs like musigi, pel, lide (?) (and others). Opera makes her cry. ("Opera drives her to tears.")

tuv.seg: Lalayen pel te na wawa.
The singer makes her cry.

tu.note: [yamgi vs yamgibe] The singer makes her cry. The boss makes her cry.

tuv.seg: Filmekef musigi atoyen na wawa.
The director had the actress cry. (obliged her to cry)

tu.note: [sangu (hide) to be recategorized as transitive; atex (burn) and teslimu (surrender) to remain ambitransitive] sesangu - intr: hide (oneself) By the way, remember that in practice se- verbs typically function transitively with the reflexive direct object pronoun:

tuv.seg: Mi le sangu se.
I hid (myself).

tu.note: [Various meanings of "for": cel, tas, fol, fe] The preposition fol means "according to". It can be translated as "for", but only in this sense ("according to one's opinion or view"). For me, this is the most beautiful animal.

tuv.seg: Fol mi, hinto sen maxmo meli hewan.

Now notice how the meaning of "for" in the following sentences is different from those described above: "This medicine works for humans", "This is good for you", "For children, the risk is great", "For me, 40 degrees is too warm" ("For me" as in how it affects my body personally, rather than as an opinion in general).

tu.note: [Grammar addition: Colon Questions] ### Colon Questions Colon questions in Globasa are as follows.

tuv.seg: Yu suki keto: kafe or cay?
"You like what: coffee or tea?"

tu.note: [Grammar addition: Colon Questions] "You like what: coffee or tea?" Do you like coffee or tea?

tuv.seg: Yu ogar keloka: in Barati or Indonesi?
"You live where: in India or Indonesia?"

tu.note: [Revised "Omission of Verb Particles"] If I eat the apple (in the future), I will no longer be hungry.

tuv.seg: Eger te le yam yusu pingo, kam yu xa is gadibu?
If he ate your apple (in the past), will you be angry?

tu.note: [Content Words page up-to-date with new Verb Categories] You're reading (an article). She's singing (a beautiful song).

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] Globasa's compound tenses include the following perfect (completed) tenses. Present Completed: nun le

tuv.seg: Mi nun le yam pingo.
I have eaten the apple.

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] I have eaten the apple. Past Completed: le le

tuv.seg: Mi le le yam pingo.
I had eaten the apple.

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] I had eaten the apple. Future Completed: xa le

tuv.seg: Mi xa le yam pingo.
I will have eaten the apple.

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] "I have always guided him" The adverb dupul is also used with stative verbs (verbal and adjectival):

tuv.seg: Mi dupul kone te dur 30 nyan.
I have known him for 30 years.

tu.note: [basa vs loga vs eskri and the names of languages as verbs] By the way, the preposition fe should logically be used here. (I think I have "loga Globasa" in the website, so this would actually be an adjustment.)

tuv.seg: Mi loga fe Espanisa.
Mi speak (in) Spanish.

tu.note: [Prefix proposal: nen-] We currently use the word no as a prefix meaning un- (and all other variations). Whereas this is fine with adjectives, in the case of verbs (including stative) verbs, there's a slight ambiguity that can arise, if not in writing at least in speech:

tuv.seg: Mi no kox.
I am not happy.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] * Verb Complements I like to sing.

tuv.seg: Mi musi na ergo.
I must work. *or* I have to work.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] I like to sing. I must work. or I have to work.

tuv.seg: Mi no abil na danse.
I cannot dance.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] I must work. or I have to work. I cannot dance.

tuv.seg: Gitara asan na soti.
The guitar is easy to play.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] I cannot dance. The guitar is easy to play.

tuv.seg: Mi jumbi na idi.
I am ready to go. ​

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] With copula is* sentences as shown above: In these sentences, the infinitive verb phrase may be moved to the end of the sentence if it is not already in that position.

tuv.seg: Cele is na triunfa.
The goal is to win.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] The goal is to win. To be impatient is a problem.

tuv.seg: Is problem na sabarkal.
It is a problem to be impatient.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] To play the guitar is easy. or Playing the guitar is easy.

tuv.seg: Asan na soti gitara.
It is easy to play the guitar.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] To play the guitar is easy. or Playing the guitar is easy. It is easy to play the guitar.

tuv.seg: Na suyon in bahari amusane.
To swim in the sea is fun. *or* Swimming in the sea is fun.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] It is easy to play the guitar. To swim in the sea is fun. or Swimming in the sea is fun.

tuv.seg: Amusane na suyon in bahari.
It is fun to swim in the sea.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] * As the complement of a preposition: fe tayday de na danse - Instead of dancing

tuv.seg: Te le sokutu dur na danse.
He fell while dancing.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] fe tayday de na danse - Instead of dancing He fell while dancing.

tuv.seg: Fe na doxo, nini le xorsomno.
Reading, the boy fell asleep.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] The last portion (as the complement of a preposition) is a slight adjustment. Previously, the infinitive was not used after a preposition. This, however, creates an ambiguity.

tuv.seg: Te le sokutu dur danse.
He fell during the dance. (not necessarily while he was dancing)

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] He fell during the dance. (not necessarily while he was dancing) He fell while dancing. (while he was dancing)

tuv.seg: Fe doxo, nini le xorsomno.
At the reading, the boy fell asleep. (the boy wasn't necessarily the reader)

tu.note: [Grammar Adjustment Proposal: iji... ji; oro... or...; noro... nor....] nor... nor... - neither.... nor... The idea is borrowed from Esperanto, and although in works well in Esperanto, it doesn't work as well in Globasa due to nouns and verbs having the same form. For example, in direct object position ji (both) can easily be interpreted to mean "and" even after the object has been uttered.

tuv.seg: Mi estudi ji danse ji lala.
I study both dance and song, or I study and dance and sing.

tu.note: [Suiwol Kraw (First original story in Globasa)] but the water was at the bottom. It thought for some time.

tuv.seg: Te preporta bannumer lilpetra ji
It brought some pebbles and

tu.note: [Suiwol Kraw (First original story in Globasa)] It thought for some time. It brought some pebbles and

tuv.seg: plasi oto fe inya de kaxa.
placed them in the container.

tu.note: [Suiwol Kraw (First original story in Globasa)] The water came up. It drank the water.

tuv.seg: Kox, te awfley.
Happy, it flew away.

tu.note: [Updated ke vs ku- correlatives section] You might notice the different ways of saying "like/as". You are like me.

tuv.seg: Kupul mi, pia te ergo in kitabudom.
Like me, she too works at the library.

tu.note: [Updated ke vs ku- correlatives section] Mi salom yu kuli misu sodar. (I had "kupul" previously, but I think "kuli" makes more sense here.) I greet you as my brother.

tuv.seg: Kumaner mi le loga...
Like I said...

tu.note: [Grammar Adjustment: ke- vs. ku- correlatives] Formerly, ke- correlatives were used only in direct questions other than kam (yes/no) questions. ku- correlatives were used only in statements. In spite of being a simple division of labor for ke- and ku- correlatives, this does not appear to work well in practice. For example, the following sentence is ambiguous, just as it is in English (although English differentiates by whether or not who is stressed):

tuv.seg: Mi le swal tas misu tie kute suki cokolateli keke.
I asked my uncle who likes chocolate cake.

tu.note: [Grammar Adjustment Proposal: extending use of "-su" as genitive particle for all nouns] Currently, the suffix -su is used as a possessive adjective marker applied to pronouns. It seems inevitable that -su would end up being experimentally used for nouns as well. I suggest we make -su official for this use, but apply it as a separate word, rather than a suffix. As a separate word, proper nouns would remain intact in form as well as in pronunciation of stress.

tuv.seg: Maria su baytu kijawi. = Baytu de Maria kijawi.
Mary's house is green.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] Currently the words for today (nundina), yesterday (leja dina or ledina) and tomorrow (xaja dina or xadina) can be used as either nouns or adverbs.

tuv.seg: Mi le yuxi pedabol ledina.
I played soccer yesterday.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] Currently the words for today (nundina), yesterday (leja dina or ledina) and tomorrow (xaja dina or xadina) can be used as either nouns or adverbs. I played soccer yesterday.

tuv.seg: Ledina le is bono dina.
Yesterday was a good day.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] I played soccer yesterday. This would parallel sentences such as the following:

tuv.seg: Mi le yuxi pedabol fe dina dua.
I played soccer on Tuesday.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] This would parallel sentences such as the following: I played soccer on Tuesday.

tuv.seg: Te xa preata fe dina lima.
He will arrive (on) Friday.

Siri-Logane Tutum
The Secret-Telling Heart
To sen sati!
It's true!
Mi le sen daymo, daymo ansyapul, ji mi haji sen denpul, mas yu fikir ki mi sen majnuni keseba?
I was very, very scared, and I still am, but why do you think that I'm crazy?
Misu bimarya le balagi misu gancikowa.
My disease strengthened my senses.
To le no destrui or daifugi oto.
It didn't destroy or weaken them.
Misu maxim bala gancikowa le sen misu oreya.
My strongest sense was my hearing.
Mi le abil na ore moyto in Janatu ji in Dunya.
I could hear everything in Heaven and on Earth.
Mi le ore multi xey in Jahanom.
I heard many things in Hell.
Finto, mi sen majnuni kemaner?
So, how am I crazy?
Am juiore, ji am jui ku mi abil na kemo trankwilo ji mingu loga tas yu total hikaye.
Listen up, and pay attention to how calmly and clearly I can tell you the whole story.
Mi no jixi ku idey le ofata keloka, mas denwatu hu to le precu, to le kostante lawfen mi.
I don't know where the idea came from, but when it appeared, it constantly bothered me.
Le no hay seba kos to.
There was no reason for it.
Le no hay bala ganjon tem to.
There was no strong feeling about it.
Fe fato, mi le suki lao manixu.
I actually liked the old man.
Te le nilwatu guton mi.
He never hurt me.
Te le nilwatu burganjongi mi.
He never made me upset.
Mi le no vole tesu pesa.
I didn't want his money.
Mi fikir ki seba le sen tesu oko!
I think that it was because of his eye!
Si, dento le sen seba!
Yes, it was that!
Un to of tesu oko okocu sim kom to de nasru, sefidemo blue oko har dambo cengu per to.
One of his eyes looked like a vulture's, a light blue eye with a thin layer over it.
Denwatu hu to le oko mi, mi le ganjoncu fobido, ji mi le karar xosu xafe xosu na morgi lao manixu cel na awgi tesu oko cel moywatu.
Whenever it looked at me, I felt scared, and I very slowly decided to kill the old man to get rid of his eye forever.
Prehay cuyotyan.
Here's the point.
Yu fikir ki mi sen majnuni.
You think that I'm crazy.
Majnuniyen jixi nilto.
Crazy people know nothing.
Mas yu le ingay na oko mi.
But you should've seen me.
Yu le ingay na oko ku mi le aksyon kemo gomyo; daymo juipul, daymo cinonpul, daymo sirili, mi le ergo!
You should've seen how cleverly I acted; very carefully, very smartly, very secretly, I worked!
Mi le nilwatu sen maxmo lutufpul tas lao manixu kom dur total safta leki mi le morgi te.
I was never nicer to the old man than during the whole week before I killed him.
Ji fe moy noce daju fe midinoce, mi le rota hantatul de tesu dwer, ji mi le buka to: o, daydenmo narem!
And every night at about midnight, I turned the latch of his door and opened it: oh, so gently!
Ji jaxali, denwatu hu mi le fale kufimo day bukaxey tas misu kapi, mi le ingi luminkal lenterna, kompletomo klosido celki nil lumin brila, ji jaxali, mi le pasgi misu kapi.
And then, when I made a hole big enough for my head, I put in a dark lantern, completely closed so no light shined out, and then I put my head through.
O, yu le ingay na oko ku mi le pasgi to kemo gomyo!
Oh, you should've seen how cunningly I put it through!
Mi le harka to hanman, daymo, daymo hanman, celki mi no jundwan somno de manixu.
I moved it slowly, very, very slowly, so I wouldn't disrupt the old man's sleep.
Mi le pasa un satu cel na kufi pasgi misu kapi celki mi abil na oko te durki te le leta per sesu bistar.
It took me an hour to put my head through enough so that I could see him as he laid on his bed.
Ha!
Hah!
Kam majnuniyen ger le sen denmo gomyo kom hinto?
Would a crazy person have been as clever as this?
Ji jaxali, denwatu hu misu kapi le kompleto sen in kamer, mi le buka lenterna juipul, daymo juipul (koski bisagra le soti); mi le kufi buka to celki dambo radya fe lumin celidi oko de nasru.
And then when my head was fully in the room, I opened the lantern carefully, very carefully (because the hinges made noise); I opened it just enough for a thin ray of light to reach the vulture eye.
Ji mi le fale hinto dur sabe noce, moy noce preciso fe midinoce, mas mi le oko ki oko moywatu sen klosido; fe folo, na fale ergo le sen nenible.
And I did this for seven long nights, every night at exactly midnight, but I saw that the eye was always closed, so it was impossible to do the work.
To le no sen lao manixu hu da le lawfen mi; to le sen tesu Bur Oko.
It wasn't the old man that bothered me; it was his Evil Eye.
Ji fe moy soba, denwatu hu dinlumin le ata, mi le sexinloypul inidi kamer, ji mi le yunkipul pala tas te, le kweho voka tesu name ji le swal ku tesu noce sen kepul.
And every morning, when the daylight came, I confidently entered the room and spoke boldly to him, cheerfully calling him by name, and asked how his night was.
Te ger le musi na sen daymo cinonpul cel na gixim ki fe moy noce preciso fe midinoce, mi juioko te durki te somno.
He'd have to be really smart to find out that every night at exactly midnight, I looked at him while he slept.
Fe ocoyum noce, mi le sen maxmo juipul kom xugwanpul denwatu hu mi le buka dwer.
On the eighth night, I was more cautious than usual when I opened the door.
Mi le harka misu hanta maxmo hanman kom minuto-ixara de satumeter.
I moved my hand more slowly than a watch's minute hand.
Mi le nilwatu xoraham daraje de misu abilya ji sofi denpul kom fe den noce.
I never realized the extent of my abilities and wisdom like I did that night.
Mi le eskaso abil na krasi misu ganjon fe triunfa.
I could hardly contain my feeling of triumph.
Am imaje mi fe na buka dwer xosu xafe xosu, ji te fe na sen ixikal fe misu sirili aksyon ji fikir.
Imagine me opening the door little by little, and him being unaware of my secret actions and thoughts.
Mi le bankwanti lilhaha kos den idey, ji te le ible ore mi koski te le abruto harka per sesu bistar kwasimo surprisado.
I somewhat chuckled at the idea, and he might have heard me because he suddenly moved on the bed as if startled.
Yu ible fikir ki mi le rukadam, mas no.
You might think that I retreated, but no.
Tesu kamer le sen kompletomo luminkal (janela le sen tangemo klosido kos fobi fe ofcoriyen), ji kos to, mi le jixi ki te no abil na oko dwer fe na buka, ji mi le duregi na pel to hanman, hanman.
His room was completely dark (the windows were tightly closed because of a fear of robbers), and so I knew that he couldn't see the door opening, and I kept pushing it steadily, steadily.
Misu kapi le sen fe inya, ji mi le jaxa buka lenterna, denwatu hu misu dayxuji deleza per estanoli liftitul, ji lao manixu le sidecu per bistar, fe na dayloga, "Kete sen denloka!?"
My head was inside, and I was about to open the lantern when my thumb slipped on the tin lever, and the old man sat up in the bed, shouting, "Who's there!?"
Mi le resta totalmo harkakal ji le loga nilto.
I kept quite still and said nothing.
Fe total satu, mi le no harka adola, ji fe durya, mi le no ore te na letacu.
For a whole hour I did not move a muscle, and in the meantime, I did not hear him lie down.
Te le haji side per bistar, fe na ore, preciso denmaner hu mi le fale to fe moy noce, dur na ore gubangu in divar.
He still sat in the bed, listening, just as I did night after night, listening to the beetles in the wall.
Nerxali, mi le ore daifu exnafasu, ji mi le jixi ki to sen exnafasu fe teror.
Soon, I heard a weak exhale, and I knew that it was the exhale of terror.
To le no sen exnafasu fe guton or hazuniya, o no!
It wasn't an exhale of pain or sadness, oh no!
To le sen sotilil, inhifazido soti hu da exata of amikuya de ruho denwatu hu to sen pul fe fobi.
It was the quiet, held-in sound that comes from the bottom of the soul when filled with fear.
Mi le kone hin soti bon.
I knew that sound well.
Fe multi noce, preciso fe midinoce, denwatu hu moyte le somno, to le xunjan in misu cati, fe na maxgi fobi hu da le lawfen mi yon sesu rusoti.
Many nights, at exactly midnight, when everyone was asleep, it grew in my chest, increasing the fears that bothered me with its frightening echo.
Mi loga tas yu, mi le kone to bon.
I tell you, I knew it well.
Mi le jixi ku lao manixu ganjon keto, ji mi le ganjon simpati tas te, fe hataya ki mi le sirili fikir ki to sen humorpul.
I knew what the old man felt, and pitied him, although I secretly thought that it was funny.
Mi le jixi ki te sen jage xorfe unyum lil soti hu denwatu te le jwan in bistar.
I knew that he had been awake since the first slight noise when he turned in bed.
Tesu plu fobi le xunjan xorfe denwatu.
His fears had been growing since then.
Te le xidu na imanugi se ki oto sen basikal, mas te le no sukses.
He had tried to convince himself that they were baseless, but he couldn't.

Te le loga tas se, "To sen sol vento in dudantubo, to sen sol maux hu da trasidi dixan," or "To sen sol krigiri hu da le fale un solo krigirisa." Si, te le xidu na anwi se yon hin plu jadin, mas te le no xorhare sukses.

He had been telling himself, "It's just the wind in the chimney, it's just a mouse crossing the floor," or "It's just a cricket that made a single chirp." Yes, he has been trying to comfort himself with these suppositions, but he had no success.
To le no funsyon koski Morya, durki te le nercu cel te, le fale sesu luminkal saye fe fronta de te, ji Morya le lifafa te in to.
It didn't work because Death, as he approached him, made his dark shadow in front of him and wrapped him in it.
Ji den nenokodo saye le kosa ki te ganci misu presen in kamer, fe hataya ki te le noro oko nor ore mi.
And that unseen shadow made him sense, although he neither saw nor heard, my presence in the room.
Xafe na intizar daymo sabar dur lungo watu wal na ore te na letacu, mi le karar na buka daylil daraki in lenterna.
After waiting very patiently for a long time without hearing him lie down, I decided to open a very small crevice in the lantern.
Mi le buka to daymo, daymo juipul finki un solo luminlil radya, denpul kom xilo de kumi, le exidi daraki ji le celidi nasruli oko.
So I opened it very, very carefully until a single dim ray, like the thread of a spider, came out of the crevice and reached the vulture eye.
To le sen pahnamo bukado, ji mi le sencu gadibu denwatu hu mi le juioko to.
It was widely open, and I got angry when I looked at it.
Mi le oko to perfeto.
I saw it perfectly.

To le sen daifumo blue har ajabu koberi per to hu da le day fobi mi, mas mi le no abil na oko resta de muka or jismu de lao manixu koski mi le lide radya preciso cel sahi lokabage wal na musi na fikir.

It was a dull blue with a strange covering over it that really frightened me, but I couldn't see the rest of the old man's face or body because I directed the ray at exactly the right spot without having to think.
Ji kam yu memori to hu denwatu mi le loga ki dento hu yu fikir ki da sen majnuniya sen sol maxboncu fe gancikowa?
And remember when I said that what you think is craziness is just increased senses?
Nunto, mi le ore lil, velosi soti, denpul kom satumeter lifafado in koton.
Well, I heard a brief little sound, like a watch wrapped in cotton.
Mi le kone pia den soti.
I knew that sound well, too.
To le sen nabiza de tutum de lao manixu.
It was the beating of the old man's heart.
To le sengi mi maxmo gadibu, denmaner hu darbe fe drumu yunki askeriyen.
It made me angrier, like how the beating of a drum encourages a soldier.
Mas fe hataya fe dento, mi le estowoju mi ji le resta harkakal.
But despite that, I resisted and stayed still.
Mi le eskaso nafasu.
I barely breathed.
Mi le restagi lenterna harkakal.
I kept the lantern still.
Mi le jaribi ku mi abil na restagi radya kemo harkakal per oko.
I tested how still I could keep the ray on the eye.
Fe durya, nabiza de tutum le maxbalacu.
Meanwhile, the beating of the heart increased.
To le sencu maxmo ji maxmo velosi, maxmo ji maxmo sotipul, sekundo xafe sekundo.
It became faster and faster, louder and louder, every moment.
Manixu le dayible sen kompletomo dayfobido!
The man must have been absolutely terrified!
To le sencu maxmo sotipul, mi riloga, maxmo sotipul, fol moyun sekundo!
It grew louder, I repeat, louder, every second!
Kam yu aham mi?
Do you understand me?
Mi le uje zekaru ki mi asan sencu fobido, to sen sati.
I already mentioned that I easily get scared, and I am.
Ji fe midiya de noce, in fobine sotikalya de den lama baytu, daydenmo ajabu soti le kompleto fobi mi.
And in the middle of the night, in the dreadful silence of that old house, such a strange noise completely terrified me.
Hatali, mi le resta harkakal dur bannumer maxpul minuto.
Even so, I kept still for a few more minutes.
Mas nabiza le sencu maxmo ji maxmo sotipul!
But the beating got louder and louder!
Mi le fikir ki tutum xa pom.
I thought the heart would burst.
Ji jaxali, neo banto le yolyu mi: soti ible beore jara!
And then something new worried me: the sound might be heard by a neighbor!
Watu fe morcu de lao manixu le preata!
The time of the old man's death had come!
Ton sotipul cihe, mi le buka lenterna ji le tyao cel in kamer.
With a loud yell, I opened the lantern and jumped into the room.
Te le ayay un mara, ji sol un mara.
He screamed once, and only once.
Jaxali momento, mi le pospel te cel dixan ji le plasi wazenpul bistar per te.
The next moment, I pulled him to the floor and put the heavy bed on top of him.
Jaxali, mi le tabasum kweho, fe na jixi ki fale kriban sen finido.
Then I smiled cheerfully, knowing that the deed was almost finished.
Mas dur multi minuto, tutum le duregi na nabiza har koberido soti.
But for many minutes, the heart kept beating with a muffled sound.
Hatali, hinto le no lawfen mi koski to ger no beore pas divar.
This, however, didn't bother me, as it wouldn't be heard through the wall.
Fe fini, to le esto.
Finally, it stopped.
Lao manixu le sen mor.
The old man was dead.
Mi le harka bistar ji le moni morjismu.
I moved the bed and examined the corpse.
Si, te le sen kompletomo, kompletomo mor.
Yes, he was completely, completely dead.
Mi le plasi misu hanta per tesu tutum ji le restagi to denloka dur multi minuto.
I put my hand on his heart and kept it there for many minutes.
Le no hay nabiza.
There was no pulse.
Te le sen kompletomo mor.
He was completely dead.
Tesu oko le no haji lawfen mi.
His eye would not bother me anymore.
Eger yu haji fikir ki mi sen majnuni, yu xa no haji fikir dento denwatu hu mi xa tosifu gomyo xey hu mi le fale da cel na sangu jismu.
If you still think I'm crazy, you won't think that anymore when I describe the clever things I did to hide the body.
Durki noce le pasa, mi le ergo velosi mas sotikal.
As the night passed, I worked quickly but quietly.
Mi le ofplasi tiga tahta of dixan de kamer ji le plasi moyto in neo bukaxey.
I removed three planks from the floor of the room and put everything in the opening.
Jaxali, mi le ruplasi tahta daydenmo gomyo, ki fe folo nil insanli oko, no hata tesu to, ger abil na xorjui mal banto.
Then, I put the boards back so cunningly that no human eye, not even his, could have noticed anything wrong.
Le hay nilto na safegi.
There was nothing to clean.
Nil burtyan, nil damuplax.
No stains, no blood splatters.
Mi le sen godomo juipul tem dento.
I was too cautious for that.
Xaki mi le fini misu ergo, to le sen satu care, haji denmo luminkal kom midinoce.
After I finished my work, it was four o'clock, still as dark as midnight.
Denwatu hu satu le rinjon, le hay toka per dwer fe fronta.
When the bell rang at the hour, there was a knock at the front door.
Mi le joxupul idi cel na buka to, koski mi le hare keto na befobi fe nunya?
I cheerfully went to open it, because what did I have now to fear?
Tiga manixu le inidi, hu da adebupul xorkonegi se denpul kom polisiyen.
Three men entered, who politely introduced themselves as police officers.
Ayay le beore jara dur noce hu da maxgi fikir ki bur banto le befale; informe le begibe tas polisidom, ji polisiyen le beirsal cel na ofxerca zona.

A scream had been heard by a neighbor during the night, increasing suspicions that something bad was done; information was given to the police station, and they (the officers) were sent to search the area.
Mi le tabasum, koski mi le hare keto na befobi?
I smiled, because what did I have to fear?
Mi le bonatagi manixu.
I welcomed the men.
Mi le loga tas ete ki cihe le sen kos misu roya, ji ki lao manixu sen awsenli in nongyogeo.
I told them that the scream was from my dream, and that the old man was away in the countryside.
Mi le gida misu visitayen wey baytu.
I guided my visitors around the house.
Mi le loga tas ete ki ete am xerca, ji am xerca bon.
I told them to search, and to search well.
Fe fini, mi le gida ete cel tesu kamer.
Finally, I guided them to his room.
Mi le onexa tas ete tesu jacipulxey, anjen ji nenharkado.
I showed them his valuables, safe and unmoved.
Daymo sexinloypul, mi le preporta kursi cel in kamer ji le teyan ki ete am sidecu ji laxocu, durki mi, fe na ganjoncu triunfapul, le plasi misu kursi supra to hu denloka morjismu de korbani le leta.
Very confidently, I brought chairs into the room and offered them to sit down and relax, while I, feeling victorious, placed my chair above where the victim's corpse lay.
Polisiyen le sen truti.
The officers were satisfied.
Misu konduta le imanugi ete.
My behavior convinced them.
Mi le sen juilayemo estreskal.
I was remarkably unstressed.
Ete le sidecu, ji durki mi le jawabu kweho, imi le intrepala ordinari.
They sat down, and while I responded cheerfully, we conversed casually.
Mas nerxali, mi le xoru na sencu cambay ji le vole ki ete am awidi.
But soon, I started to become pale and wanted them to leave.
Misu kapi le guton, ji mi le fikir ki mi ore rinjon in misu ore; mas ete le duregi na pala.
My head hurt, and I thought that I heard a ringing in my ears; but they kept talking.
Rinjon le sencu maxmo ji maxmo xorjuiible.
The ringing became more and more noticeable.
Mi le pala maxmo huru cel na esto ganjon, mas to le dure ji sencu hata maxmo xorjuiible, finki finili, mi le xoraham ki soti no ofata misu ore.
I talked more freely to stop the feeling, but it continued and became even more noticeable, until finally, I realized that the noise did not come from my ears.
Mi le xankakal sencu cambay, mas mi le pala maxmo velosi ji sotipul.
I definitely became very pale, but I talked more quickly and loudly.
Soti le sencu maxmo sotipul, ji mi le no jixi ku na fale keto.
The sound became louder, and I didn't know what to do.
To le sen sotikal, nenmingu, velosi soti, denpul kom satumeter koberido in koton.
It was a quiet, covered, fast sound, like a watch wrapped in cotton.
Mi le velosi nafasu, fe hataya ki polisiyen le no ore to.
I breathed quickly, even though the officers didn't hear it.
Mi le pala maxmo velosi ji maxmo joxupul, mas soti le foldarajeli sencu maxmo sotipul.
I spoke faster and more passionately, but the sound gradually became louder.
Mi le estaycu ji xijere tem nenmuhim xey, sotipul ji yon day jestu, mas soti le foldarajeli sencu maxmo sotipul.
I stood up and argued about unimportant things loudly and with big gestures, but the noise gradually became louder.
Ete xa no awidi keseba?
Why wouldn't they leave?
Mi le anda suo ji kanan yon day kadam, kwas mi le sencu gadibu kos etesu komenta, mas soti le foldarajeli sencu maxmo sotipul.
I walked back and forth with heavy steps, as if I got angry with their comments, but the sound gradually became louder.
O Teo!
Oh God!
Mi ger abil na fale keto?
What could I do?
Mi le paniko, mi le gadibu pala, mi le burlexi!
I panicked, I talked angrily, I swore!
Mi le hantacudu kursi hu mi le side per da ji le garu tahta yon to, mas umumi, soti le durepul sencu maxmo sotipul.
I grabbed the chair that I sat on and scraped it against the boards, but the sound continuously became louder overall.
To le sencu maxmo sotipul, maxmo sotipul, maxmo sotipul!
It became louder, louder, louder!
Ji ete le haji pala yukwe ji le tabasum.
And they still talked pleasantly and smiled.
Kam to le sen ible ki ete no ore to?
Was it possible that they didn't hear it?
Moyabil Teo!
Almighty God!
No, no!
No, no!
Ete le ore to!
They heard it!
Ete le gixim banto!
They suspected something!
Ete le jixi!
They knew!
Ete le coxo misu teror!
They mocked my terror!
Mi le fikir dento, ji mi haji fikir dento.
That's what I thought, and that's what I still think.
Mas he banto le sen maxmo bon kom hin suferi!
But anything was better than this suffering!
He banto le sen maxmo tahamulible kom hin coxo!
Anything was more tolerable than this mockery!
Mi le no haji abil na tahamul den sewdo tabasum!
I couldn't tolerate those fake smiles anymore!
Mi le ganjon ki mi musi na ayay or morcu!
I felt that I had to scream or die!
Ji fe nunya, ripul, am juiore!
And now, once again, listen!
Maxmo sotipul!
Louder!
Maxmo sotipul!
Louder!
Maxmo sotipul!
Louder!
Maxmo sotipul!
Louder!
"Uyu, buryen!" mi le dayloga, "Am esto na kwasigi! Mi etiraf krimen! Am ofplasi tahta! Hinloka, hinloka! To sen nabiza de tesu daybur tutum!"
"Villains!" I screamed, "Stop pretending! I admit the crime! Remove the boards! Here, here! It's the beating of his terrible heart!"
